slides.texte_overlay:
7 social hacks that feel
illegal to know

Forgot someone's name? Introduce them to a friend. "Have you two met?" They'll say their own name out loud, and you never have to admit you forgot it. Works every single time, and nobody ever notices.
Need a favor from a busy person? Make it tiny and specific. Not "Can you help me?" but "Can you look at one paragraph for two minutes?" Small asks get a yes. Vague ones get a "maybe later."
Want an honest opinion? Ask "What would you change?" instead of "What do you think?" People are too polite to criticize, but they love to suggest improvements. That's where the real feedback is.
Always have one interesting thing to share. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. "Did you know Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the pyramids?" Instant conversation.
slides.texte_sophia: Always have one interesting thing to share. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll never be the one stuck for something to say.

slides.texte_overlay: Walk into a room where you know nobody? Find the person standing alone and say "I don't know anyone here either, mind if I join you?" You just saved two people from an awkward night.

When a conversation stalls, don't ask a new question. Repeat their last few words back, like a question. "You moved to Lisbon?" They'll keep talking, and you'll look like the best listener in the room.
When someone apologizes for being late, don't say "It's fine." Say "Thanks for coming." Same moment, but now they feel welcome instead of guilty. People remember how you made the small moments feel.
